rules.sentence: Middle aortic syndrome (MAS) is a rare disease characterized by segmental or diffuse narrowing of the abdominal and/or distal descending aorta with involvement of the renal and visceral branches and represents an important cause of severe hypertension in children.
Ostial stenosis of the major branches of the proximal abdominal aorta is a characteristic in MAS.
MAS was described for the first time in 1963 by Sen et al in 16 patients with inflammatory narrowing of the middle aortic segment.
It represents 0.5–2% of all cases of aortic narrowing.
Most cases of MAS are idiopathic, but MAS may occur in genetic and acquired disorders (Table 1).
